clue.text: Fail to justify almost a religious conviction

indicators.note: almost tells us to stop one letter short of the full word for the conviction

parts.note: a belief is a religious conviction

explanation.surface: Someone's faith turns out not to be well founded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the final F from BELIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: To belie something is to show it false or fail to bear it out.

clue.text: Garment for a music presenter appearing first in Tennyson's tragedy

indicators.note: the presenter and the a go inside the play's title

parts.note: Becket is a verse tragedy by Tennyson about Thomas Becket

indicators.note: the presenter comes before the a, so it is placed ahead of it

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, presents music

explanation.surface: Someone seeks an outfit for a DJ starring in a Tennyson play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing first' puts DJ before A, and 'in' places DJA inside BECKET.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed jacket is a short jacket worn over a nightdress when sitting up in bed.

clue.text: One defeated in a close race

indicators.note: in tells us the word sits inside the run of letters across close and race

explanation.surface: A runner narrowly beaten in a tight contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a description of the runner-up, but the word is concealed across 'close race'.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever is beaten in a contest, however narrowly, is the one who did not win.

clue.text: With which we observe the old society in 8

indicators.note: the old word and the society letter go inside the answer to 8

parts.note: the answer to 8 down, a crew, is eight
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: Old club members watch something in a group of eight.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 points to the answer of 8 down, EIGHT; 'the old' is YE, and with S (society) it goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is the faculty of seeing, the means by which people look at things.

clue.text: Soldiers imprisoning the learned in a different state

indicators.note: the soldiers lock up the word the, so it goes between their two letters

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers
taken as written
wise means learned or knowledgeable

explanation.surface: Troops lock up scholars somewhere far from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoning' puts THE between the O and R of OR (other ranks); WISE (learned) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means in another manner or condition, so it serves as an adverbial phrase for a changed situation.

clue.text: Sluggish exudation, say, from this river

indicators.note: say means the word for slow seepage is spoken, matching the river's name

parts.note: ooze is a slow seeping out

explanation.surface: Slow seepage comes from a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in England, several of them in fact; it is said just like OOZE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is an English river flowing through York.

clue.text: Sheer folly, holding a fight in this neighbourhood

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the fight inside them
folly suggests madness, so the letters of the word sheer are jumbled

parts.note: a bout is a boxing fight

explanation.surface: Sheer madness to start a brawl around here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'folly' rearranges SHEER into HERES, and 'holding' puts A BOUT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereabouts means near this place, in the local area.

clue.text: In a game it precedes nearly all the regular procedure

indicators.note: this piece comes before the shortened word all
the word it goes inside the game's abbreviation

parts.note: RU is rugby union
taken as written

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter of all is dropped

explanation.surface: In a sporting contest, one thing comes before almost everything as a set routine.
explanation.walkthrough: IT goes 'In' RU (rugby union) to give RITU, which 'precedes' AL, ALL 'nearly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual is a fixed order of actions followed every time, a set ceremony.

clue.text: A citizen put up in it with a lover

indicators.note: the overturned citizen is placed inside the word it
in a down clue put up means the citizen is written bottom to top

parts.note: a Roman is a citizen of Rome

explanation.surface: A city dweller is installed with a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns A ROMAN into NAMORA, which goes 'in' IT; the final A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman who is loved, a sweetheart or mistress.

clue.text: Crew identifying this clue?

definitions.meaning: the clue is numbered 8, so this word names it

explanation.surface: A rowing team labels its own clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing boat's team of oarsmen is called by its number; and this clue's number is the same figure.

clue.text: Possible source of cash for a female poet

parts.note: Di, short for Diana, is a female name
Edmund Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene

explanation.surface: A woman poet looks around for somewhere to get money.
explanation.walkthrough: The female is a girl's name, DI, and the poet is Edmund Spenser.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash machine dispenses money, so it is one example of a device that hands out notes.

clue.text: Nasal tone of six-footer returning to keep wicket

indicators.note: the reversed insect holds the wicket letter inside it
returning asks for the insect's name to be read from right to left

parts.note: a gnat is an insect, and insects have six feet
W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: An insect with a whine comes back to guard the stumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns GNAT into TANG, and 'to keep' puts W (wicket, in cricket scoring) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a resonant nasal quality in someone's voice or accent.

clue.text: Fearful of a noisy 15

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical marking for loud
the answer to 15 down is a sudden attack, another word for which is raid

explanation.surface: Someone dreads a loud assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 points to the answer of 15 down, an attack, which here gives RAID; 'noisy' is F, forte in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Being scared means being frightened or apprehensive, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Lazy fellow's design to capture a bishop

indicators.note: the design surrounds the bishop as a chess piece would be captured

parts.note: a layout is a planned design or arrangement
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: An idler has a plan to take a chess bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to capture' puts A and B (bishop) inside LAYOUT; 'fellow's' supplies the possessive link.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler who avoids work is a slacker, the kind of loafer this word describes.

clue.text: Exhibit clothing for the equestrian sports person

parts.note: to show is to exhibit
a jumper is a knitted sweater, an item of clothing

explanation.surface: Displaying riding gear for a horse-sport competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like a verb but is a noun, a JUMPER (British for a sweater).
explanation.definitionFit: A rider who competes over fences in arena events is a competitor in that discipline.

clue.text: Dark head covering given by king to Thomas More?

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
night is the dark time
a hood covers the head

explanation.surface: A monarch hands a black cowl to the Tudor statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the king giving More a hood; in fact K goes before NIGHT and HOOD, and Sir Thomas More is an example of the honour's holder, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More was dubbed a knight, so he exemplifies the honour conferred by the Crown.

clue.text: Attack in Jerusalem bottled up police

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the police letters read bottom to top

parts.note: RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary
Sion, or Zion, stands for Jerusalem

explanation.surface: An assault in Jerusalem kept the police contained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RUC into CUR, which is 'bottled' at the front of SION, after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An incursion is a hostile raid into territory, a sudden invasion.

clue.text: Writer married in a research building

indicators.note: the married letter sits inside the word for the building

parts.note: a lab, short for laboratory, is a building for research

explanation.surface: An author gets wed inside a science laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb was an English essayist; M (married) goes inside LAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia, so he is an example of an author.

clue.text: Cooks hog's head, having accepted a woman's money

indicators.note: the cooking word takes the woman's pronoun inside it

parts.note: bakes means cooks in an oven
she is the pronoun for a woman

indicators.note: head means the first letter of hog

explanation.surface: Someone roasts a pig's head after taking a lady's cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having accepted' puts SHE inside BAKES, and H is the 'head' of hog.
explanation.definitionFit: Baksheesh is a tip or bribe, a gift of cash.

clue.text: Cutting caper, initially jumping on one foot

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of caper

parts.note: hopping is jumping on one leg

explanation.surface: A slicing dance step, leaping on one leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caper' looks like part of the definition, a dance, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping is cutting something into pieces with blows.

clue.text: Understood one is lacking in diplomacy

indicators.note: is lacking signals the numeral for one going missing from the word

parts.note: tacit means understood without being said
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a particular person has no finesse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is lacking' takes I (one) out of TACIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tact is sensitivity in dealing with people, much the same as diplomacy in its everyday sense.

clue.text: Champion put on to shoot at the fair?

indicators.note: the word for champion is attached after the word for shoot

parts.note: a switch is a thin flexible shoot or twig
to back someone is to champion them

explanation.surface: A winner is told to try the rifle range at the funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' looks like a verb but is a twig, SWITCH; BACK is 'put on to' it. The definition is by example: a switchback ride is found at a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchback is a roller-coaster ride, a typical funfair attraction.

clue.text: Lets on, foolishly, that this is hot

indicators.note: foolishly suggests the letters of lets on are muddled

explanation.surface: Someone stupidly reveals the item is stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' is slang for taken illegally.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for goods that were taken illegally.

clue.text: Exhausted, like the case of Graham Greene

definitions.meaning: worn out, with no energy left

definitions.text: like the case of Graham Greene
definitions.meaning: Greene's novel is titled A ... Case

explanation.surface: A tired novelist is compared with a book by Graham Greene.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone utterly spent is used up and depleted; and Greene's 1960 novel about a leper colony bears this word in its title.

clue.text: Sort of English degree, so it appears

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
sic, Latin for thus, marks something as written in the original

explanation.surface: A kind of English qualification, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Basic English is a simplified 850-word version of English.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic English is a simplified form of the language with a limited vocabulary.

clue.text: One watery sound quietly assimilated into another

indicators.note: the quiet letter is absorbed inside the second watery word

parts.note: another watery sound, a slosh
P is piano, the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A soft gurgle blends into a louder one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another watery sound, SLOSH; 'assimilated into' puts P (piano, quietly) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A splosh is a splash, the noise of liquid hitting something.

clue.text: Ring up an amateur broadcaster in Nebraska

parts.note: a ring is shaped like O

indicators.note: in a down clue up means these letters read bottom to top

parts.note: an gives the letter A
a ham is an amateur radio operator

explanation.surface: Someone calls a radio enthusiast in the Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns A HAM into MAHA after O (ring). Ring up looks like a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in that US state.

clue.text: Beam in a period of prosperity

definitions.meaning: a spar along the bottom of a sail

explanation.surface: A timber spar in good times.
explanation.definitionFit: A boom is a spar holding the foot of a sail; it is also a time of rapid economic growth.

clue.text: Picture of an apparatus for producing whisky

definitions.meaning: a photograph taken from a film

explanation.surface: Someone looks at a photo of distillery equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A single frame from a movie is a photograph of that name; and the copper vessel used in distilling spirits shares the word.

clue.text: Next archbishop is to wear the old cross

indicators.note: the archbishop puts on the old cross like a vestment, so it goes inside

parts.note: a primate is an archbishop, the senior bishop of a province
X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: The incoming archbishop will put on an antique crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is to wear' puts O (old) and X (cross) inside PRIMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Proximate means nearest or immediately following, so it means coming after in sequence.

clue.text: Riddle of English politician playing a French instrument

parts.note: Con is short for a Conservative, the English party member
un is French for a
a drum is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: An English MP is seen playing a French instrument, a puzzling sight.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is a Conservative; 'a French' means the French for 'a', UN.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a puzzle or tricky question.

clue.text: Hard grind for a architect, say

indicators.note: say tells us to hear the name spoken, where it matches a word with a silent G

parts.note: John Nash designed Regent Street and Brighton Pavilion

explanation.surface: An architect toils hard at a demanding task.
explanation.walkthrough: The G of the answer is silent, so it is said like NASH, the Regency architect John Nash. 'Hard grind' is grinding one's teeth hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnash is to grind the teeth together forcefully.
